acceptance: The digest of a digest-keyed exception covers only the consuming symbol plus the module-level bindings it resolves through, so an edit elsewhere in the file (for example one unrelated assertion in tests/unit/workflows/test_stacked_pr_base_guard.py) does not invalidate it and needs no separate registry PR. Tests show that an unrelated edit keeps the exception valid, and that an edit to the consumer symbol or to a module-level binding it resolves through still invalidates it.

The owner has recorded one decision: keep the two-PR flow (and document it, including the recurring cases above), or let a PR's own new exceptions count only when the required oracle-review soundness check covers the quality/comment-policy.json change. Under no option may a PR authorize its own exception without that review. If the second option is chosen, a test shows that a PR adding an exception without the review still fails, and the rule applies to exceptions, digest fixtures and pinned external notices alike.

docs/development/comment-policy.md describes the chosen procedure and states the correct count of digest fixtures: the sentence at line 90 ("The one current fixture") is replaced, because there are 68.
context: 2026-10-09 tracker review: Scope widened from the exception case to three instances of the base-only design (exceptions, digest-keyed fixtures, external pinned notices); the two-PR workaround recurs (#2824 then #2840, #2773 then #2785). Absorbs the exception ratchet item; CedarDB context (#2773/#2785) moved here. Acceptance 2 is an owner decision, not an implementation choice. Related: comment-policy-pinned-notice-drift-guard covers the separate LICENSE/COPYRIGHT.md gap.
description:
Transition mode honours a quality/comment-policy.json exception only once it is on the base commit. Three instances of this base-only design now force a two-PR flow (land the registry change first, then the real change):

1. Exceptions. scripts/check_comment_policy.py:411 keeps only exceptions that are already in baseline_policy["exceptions"]. A PR that adds a file needing an exception (the CedarDB UAT config header in #2773, landed via #2785) cannot pass until the exception is on develop.
2. Digest-keyed fixtures. Executable-payload exceptions carry a digest of the whole file's AST (python_consumer_digest, scripts/comment_syntax.py:387-399). There are 68 digest exceptions across about 40 test files. Any edit to one of these files, even one assertion, changes the digest and produces a payload-error that the same PR cannot register (tests/unit/workflows/test_stacked_pr_base_guard.py in the cut-over; #2824 then #2840).
3. External pinned notices. scripts/check_comment_policy.py:222 reads the notice pin from the base. Editing _sources/tpc-h/PATCHES.md and its pin in one PR exits 2.

The workaround recurs: #2824 then #2840, #2773 then #2785. quality/comment-policy.json is itself a soundness path, so the registry PR also needs an oracle review or a stand-in.

Constraint: no change may let a PR authorize its own comment-policy exception without the required review. Absorbs comment-policy-transition-mode-exception-ratchet, whose acceptance 1 (allow new exceptions when the same change adds or modifies files) would have let a PR self-authorize and is not carried over.
